facts.statement: Ichthyodectes is an extinct genus of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the ichthyodectid family.
facts.quote: Ichthyodectes is an extinct genus of marine ichthyodectid ray-finned fish known from the Late Cretaceous of North America & Europe.

facts.statement: A notable complete skeleton of Ichthyodectes ctenodon was officially described in 2010 after being collected by Charles H. Sternberg prior to 1919.
facts.quote: A notable specimen of I. ctenodon was collected by Charles H. Sternberg from the Smoky Hill Chalk prior to 1919 and officially described in 2010.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence of a stomach containing a smaller fish confirms that Ichthyodectes had a piscivorous diet.
facts.quote: This specimen comprises a complete individual with the skeleton of a smaller fish, most likely an Enchodus petrosus, within its stomach.

facts.statement: Ichthyodectes lived from the Cenomanian to the Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Campanian (100.5 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ichthyodectes is classified in the superorder Osteoglossomorpha, order Ichthyodectiformes, and family Ichthyodectidae.
facts.quote: superordo: Osteoglossomorpha ordo: Ichthyodectiformes familia: Ichthyodectidae

facts.statement: The species Ichthyodectes ctenodon was found in formations across Canada, the United States, and England.
facts.quote: I. ctenodon Cope, 1870 - Cenomanian of Saskatchewan, Canada (Ashville Formation), Turonian of Northwest Territories (Lac des Bois) & Alberta (Kaskapau Formation), Canada and Kansas & South Dakota, US (Carlile Shale & Niobrara Formation), Coniacian to mid-Campanian of Manitoba, Canada (Pierre Shale Formation), and late Santonian/early Campanian of Alabama, US (Mooreville Chalk).

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest that only two species can be confidently placed in the genus Ichthyodectes, with others being synonymous or belonging to different genera.
facts.quote: Although a number of species have previously been placed in the genus, more recent analyses indicate that only two species can confidently be placed in the genus, with the rest being synonymous with this species or belonging to different genera.
